previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, and recurrent urinary tract infections was admitted with fevers, chills, and malaise. She had been treated at an outside hospital with vancomycin and cefepime for suspected urosepsis. Upon transfer, she was continued on immunosuppressive therapy and switched to IV ceftriaxone based on prior sensitivities. Urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was pan-sensitive, allowing transition to oral ciprofloxacin. She remained afebrile for over 24 hours, with stable renal function and improving labs. She was discharged home to complete a 14-day course of ciprofloxacin, with plans to reassess UTI prophylaxis. Her transplant team will monitor cyclosporine levels and kidney function in follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with type 1 diabetes mellitus 
and ESRD s/p renal transplant x2 (most recently in ___ and 
history of recurrent UTIs who presented with malaise,urinary 
frequency and low grade fevers with urinary analysis consistent 
with UTI, admitted for IV antibiotics.  She was initially 
treated with ceftriaxone until speciation of her urine culture 
showed Klebsiella resistant to ceftriaxone but sensitive to 
meropenem/ertapenem. She was then transitioned to treatment with 
meropenem. Renal ultrasound with no changes noted and her 
transplant sites remained non-tender. She remained afebrile 
following this treatment. Her blood glucose ranged in the 
100-300s and was self-managed through her insulin pump. A 
midline was placed for her to continue ertapenem infusions in 
the outpatient setting for a total of 14 days of 
culture-specific treatment.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound ___, ___

FINDINGS: 

The left iliac fossa transplant renal morphology is normal.  Specifically, the
cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity, pyramids are normal, there is
no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal.  There is no
hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.75 to 0.78,
previously 0.80-0.81.  The waveform appear relatively normal with a brisk
systolic upstroke though slightly blunted peak, with antegrade diastolic flow.
The main renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke
and continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity of 101
centimeters/second, previously 141 centimeters/second.  Vascularity is
symmetric throughout transplant. The transplant renal vein is patent and shows
normal waveform.

lower quadrant renal transplant kidney.
